summary: Olvi Oyj (OLVAS.HE, NASDAQ Helsinki) makes and sells alcoholic and non-alcoholic drinks in Finland, the Baltic countries, Belarus and other European markets. Its 27.8 EUR share price gave the company a market capitalisation of EUR 573m and an enterprise value of EUR 572m on 4 November 2026, in this Valuatum market report dated 4 November 2026. Analysts forecast EUR 816m of 2028 sales and EUR 100m of operating profit. The business has no forests or property contributing separately to the price, so the share is read through the profits of three drinks operations and the small cash balance after debt and other claims.

The price is split between Rest of Europe at 12.3 EUR per share, Finland at 9.2 EUR per share and Belarus at 6.2 EUR per share, with cash less debt and other claims adding 0.0 EUR per share. Each business is priced at 5.7x its allocated 2028 operating profit: EUR 45m for Rest of Europe, EUR 33m for Finland and EUR 23m for Belarus. Together the businesses contribute 27.7 EUR per share before the balance-sheet adjustment. The allocation is based on analysts' whole-company forecasts and segment results, not separate company forecasts for each operation.

The whole company trades at 5.7x 2028 operating profit against listed industry quartiles of 5.8x, 7.6x and 11.8x. The gap reflects falling Rest of Europe volumes excluding acquisitions, weak Finnish demand and price competition, and Belarusian dividend restrictions limiting legally payable dividends to around EUR 2–4m a year. The key evidence is the 2026 result, Finnish litres sold and Belarusian margin, alongside the October 2026 operating-profit outlook of EUR 80–85m.

thesis.title: Three drinks businesses
thesis.text: The share price buys Rest of Europe, Finland and Belarus at 12.3 EUR, 9.2 EUR and 6.2 EUR per share respectively. Their 27.7 EUR total is based on forecast operating profit, with no forests or property counted separately; the price is therefore made up of operating businesses rather than hidden assets.

thesis.title: Below listed peers
thesis.text: The whole company and each business are priced at 5.7x 2028 operating profit, below the industry lower quartile of 5.8x and median of 7.6x. Weak Finnish demand, Rest of Europe losses and Belarusian dividend limits explain why the share price carries less profit multiple than comparable drinks businesses.

thesis.title: Watch volumes and profit
thesis.text: Finnish litres fell 4.4% year on year in July–September 2026, while the October 2026 company outlook was EUR 80–85m of operating profit. The next quarterly volumes, the 2026 profit result and Belarus's margin and dividend rules will determine whether the forecast profit is holding.

valuePools.name: Rest of Europe
valuePools.economics: 5.7x 2028 operating profit · EUR 45m forecast operating profit · peers 5.8x / 7.6x / 11.8x
valuePools.text: Rest of Europe sells beer and other drinks across European markets and contributes the largest part of the price at 12.3 EUR per share. The allocation gives it EUR 45m of 2028 operating profit on EUR 317m of sales, a 14% margin, and applies 5.7x operating profit. Its 2025 sales to outside customers were EUR 259m, or 39% of the company total, while the allocation gives it 44% of 2028 operating profit. The multiple is below the industry's 5.8x lower quartile, 7.6x median and 11.8x upper quartile. The main evidence against a higher reading is a 9.7% fall in volumes excluding acquisitions and heavy losses in the Danish business. Stabilising volumes in quarterly results would reduce the doubt around the forecast margin; continued declines would reinforce the cautious price.

valuePools.name: Finland
valuePools.economics: 5.7x 2028 operating profit · EUR 33m forecast operating profit · peers 5.8x / 7.6x / 11.8x
valuePools.text: Finland sells beer and alcoholic and non-alcoholic drinks to grocery retailers, restaurants and consumers, contributing 9.2 EUR per share. The allocation gives it EUR 33m of 2028 operating profit on EUR 297m of sales, an 11% margin, compared with a 12.3% margin on EUR 242m of outside sales in 2025. Its 5.7x price multiple sits just below the industry lower quartile of 5.8x. Olvi held more than 50% of the Finnish beer market in 2025, making additional volume difficult to win without price responses from competitors. July–September litres fell 4.4% to 69.4 million and operating result fell 7.6% to EUR 9.3m. Cost efficiency, the Pernod Ricard distribution range and renewed volume growth would show whether the 11% forecast margin can hold.

valuePools.name: Belarus
valuePools.economics: 5.7x 2028 operating profit · EUR 23m forecast operating profit · peers 5.8x / 7.6x / 11.8x
valuePools.text: Belarus sells beer, kvass, water, soft drinks and other beverages, contributing 6.2 EUR per share. The allocation gives it EUR 23m of 2028 operating profit on EUR 202m of sales, a margin of 11%, and applies 5.7x operating profit. The business produced EUR 164m of outside sales and 353.7 million litres in 2025, with non-alcoholic drinks accounting for 62.9% of volume. Its reported 2025 operating result was EUR 34.6m, about 21% of sales, so the allocation assumes a substantial margin decline while sales rise. Belarus is priced below the industry's 5.8x lower quartile partly because dividend rules limited legally payable dividends to around EUR 2–4m a year through the end of 2026. Margin, volume and any change in the dividend restriction determine how much of the profit reaches the parent.

coreAnalysis.heading: What the price pays for
coreAnalysis.text: The 27.8 EUR share price is an allocation across three drinks businesses rather than a claim on separately valued forests, property or other assets. Rest of Europe contributes 12.3 EUR per share, Finland 9.2 EUR and Belarus 6.2 EUR, giving 27.7 EUR before cash, debt and other claims. The balance-sheet adjustment adds 0.0 EUR per share, leaving the share price essentially supported by operating profit. The allocation uses analysts' EUR 100m 2028 whole-company operating-profit forecast and divides it between businesses using reported segment results. Rest of Europe receives EUR 45m, Finland EUR 33m and Belarus EUR 23m, each priced at 5.7x 2028 operating profit. Those figures correspond to 14% margin on EUR 317m of Rest of Europe sales, 11% on EUR 297m of Finland sales and 11% on EUR 202m of Belarus sales. The price therefore depends on all three operations delivering forecast profit, not on one dominant asset or a balance-sheet surplus. The implication for the price composition is direct: Rest of Europe is the largest pool, but Finland and Belarus together account for 15.4 EUR per share and can materially change the reading through their margins, volumes and cash-transfer constraints.

coreAnalysis.heading: Why the price is below peers
coreAnalysis.text: The 5.7x multiple applied to each business is below the industry lower quartile of 5.8x, median of 7.6x and upper quartile of 11.8x. This is not one uniform operational issue. Rest of Europe faces a 9.7% decline in volumes excluding acquisitions and heavy losses in Denmark, putting its allocated 14% 2028 margin under scrutiny. Finland reported 69.4 million litres in July–September 2026, down 4.4%, while its operating result fell 7.6% to EUR 9.3m amid price competition, weak demand, freight and packaging inflation and marketing spending. Belarus earned EUR 34.6m of operating profit in 2025, about 21% of sales, but the allocation uses an 11% 2028 margin and dividend restrictions limited legally payable dividends to around EUR 2–4m a year. Named comparisons such as Royal Unibrew at 9.4x 2028 EV/EBIT, Carlsberg at 12.1x for Finland and 12.2x for Belarus, and C&C Group at 8.3x for Rest of Europe are not like-for-like in scale or market exposure. The lower price multiple therefore reflects weaker recent evidence and harder-to-collect Belarusian profit, while peer figures are reference points rather than direct matches.

coreAnalysis.heading: What to watch
coreAnalysis.text: The next quarterly reports test whether the operating-profit assumptions behind the price can hold. Finland's 69.4 million litres in July–September 2026 were down 4.4%, so renewed growth would indicate recovery while further declines would confirm pressure on sales. The Finnish operating result should be compared with EUR 9.3m, and the explanations for weakness should be checked against price competition and freight and packaging costs. At group level, the October 2026 outlook was EUR 80–85m of operating profit, reduced from EUR 84–90m, against analysts' EUR 83m forecast. A result below EUR 80m would miss the company's own range, although reporting differences and one-off items need checking. Rest of Europe needs volume excluding acquisitions to stop falling for confidence in its 14% forecast margin to improve. Belarus requires two separate tests: whether its margin remains near the reported 2025 level of about 21% rather than the allocated 11%, and whether dividend restrictions lapse after the end of 2026. More distributable cash would change the treatment of Belarusian profit; stronger volumes and margins would change the operating-profit base. These indicators determine what the 27.8 EUR share price is made of.

risks: Finnish demand and pricing (Finland): further volume declines and price competition could reduce the allocated 11% 2028 margin, with 69.4 million litres and EUR 9.3m operating result in July–September 2026 as early warnings.

Rest of Europe volumes (Rest of Europe): volumes excluding acquisitions could continue falling from the reported 9.7% decline, weakening the forecast 14% margin; quarterly volume data is the early warning.

Belarus dividend restrictions (Belarus): rules could continue limiting legally payable dividends to around EUR 2–4m a year, leaving earned profit difficult to transfer; the year-end 2026 restriction statement is the early warning.

Group operating profit (all businesses): 2026 operating profit could fall below the October outlook's EUR 80m lower end, reducing the profit allocated across the businesses; the full-year result is the early warning.
catalysts: Finnish volume recovery (near-term, Finland): litres returning to year-on-year growth after the July–September 2026 decline of 4.4% would show that demand pressure is easing.
2026 profit delivery (near-term, all businesses): operating profit reaching the middle of the EUR 80–85m October outlook would meet analysts' EUR 83m forecast and support the allocated profit base.
Cost efficiency and Pernod Ricard distribution (medium-term, Finland): lower cost per litre or incremental sales without matching costs would support the 11% 2028 margin.
Dividend-rule change (medium-term, Belarus): expiry or relaxation of restrictions after 2026 would allow more of the business's profit to reach the parent than the current EUR 2–4m annual limit.

Margin and volume resilience (medium-term, Belarus): maintaining a margin near the reported 2025 level of about 21% and reaching about 409 million litres in 2028 would exceed the allocated 11% margin and 2028 sales case.

faqs.q: What is Olvi Oyj's share price made of?
faqs.a: The 27.8 EUR share price is allocated to Rest of Europe at 12.3 EUR per share, Finland at 9.2 EUR and Belarus at 6.2 EUR, with cash less debt and other claims adding 0.0 EUR per share. The businesses total 27.7 EUR per share before the balance-sheet adjustment.

faqs.q: Why does Olvi Oyj trade below its beverage peers?
faqs.a: Each business is priced at 5.7x 2028 operating profit, below the industry lower quartile of 5.8x and median of 7.6x. The evidence includes a 9.7% Rest of Europe volume decline excluding acquisitions, a 4.4% Finnish volume decline and Belarusian dividend limits of around EUR 2–4m a year.

faqs.q: What do analysts forecast for Olvi Oyj's sales and profit?
faqs.a: Analysts forecast EUR 816m of 2028 sales, EUR 100m of operating profit, EUR 76m of net earnings and EPS of 3.7 EUR. For 2026, the forecasts are EUR 752m of sales, EUR 83m of operating profit and EUR 61m of net earnings.

faqs.q: What should Olvi Oyj investors watch?
faqs.a: The main indicators are Finnish litres and operating result, Rest of Europe volumes excluding acquisitions, the full-year 2026 operating profit against the EUR 80–85m outlook, and Belarusian margin and dividend restrictions after the end of 2026.

faqs.q: How does Valuatum's market report work?
faqs.a: The analysis takes analysts' whole-company forecasts through 2028, allocates sales and operating profit between Finland, Rest of Europe and Belarus using reported segment results, and reads today's 27.8 EUR share price into each business using EV/EBIT comparisons with listed peers and industry quartiles.
